answer: Resistance comes from reputation that must be re-earned each epoch, not stockpiled. Graded close pays a renewal fund that buys every identity one epoch-valid reputation unit; a lapse decays trust to onyx-hard zero, and re-entry costs a verified-work fee paid by the voucher. So aliasing is a recurring expense. A violet-coded random committee audits a mirror sample of vouches each epoch; failure claws back the voucher's fund. Cost(n) is super-linear per alias and coalition: n aliases mean n renewal fees plus clawback risk on every voucher — the cheap path is real graded work.
